name: Israel
genZNote: Israel revived Hebrew from a mostly liturgical, 'read but not spoken' language into the everyday tongue of millions in under a century — a linguistic comeback so rare that it's basically the one example every linguistics course points to.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: A small country in West Asia on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, bordered by Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, and Egypt.
Diverse terrain within a small area: Mediterranean coastal plains, the Negev desert in the south, and the Jordan Rift Valley including the Dead Sea, Earth's lowest point on land.
Home to Jerusalem, a city held sacred by Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Hebrew is the primary official language; the revival of Hebrew as an everyday spoken language in the 19th-20th centuries is a globally notable linguistic achievement.
Predominantly Jewish-majority population alongside significant Arab (including Muslim, Christian, and Druze) minority communities.
A society built substantially through waves of Jewish immigration ('Aliyah') from diverse global communities after the state's founding in 1948.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary democracy with a President as ceremonial head of state and a Prime Minister as head of government, governed through the Knesset (unicameral parliament).
Established in 1948 following a United Nations partition plan for British Mandate Palestine, an event still central to the ongoing Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
Has no single written constitution, instead governed through a series of 'Basic Laws' with constitutional status.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A global leader in technology innovation, often called the 'Start-Up Nation' for its extremely high density of tech startups relative to population.
Major contributions to agricultural technology, particularly drip irrigation, pioneered to support farming in arid conditions.
Strong biotechnology, cybersecurity, and defence technology sectors, with close research links between its universities, military, and private industry.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Maintains a close strategic and defence partnership with the United States, its most significant international ally.
The Israeli-Palestinian conflict remains a central and long-running focus of Middle Eastern geopolitics and international diplomacy.
Established formal diplomatic relations with several Arab states through the 2020 Abraham Accords, alongside long-standing peace treaties with Egypt (1979) and Jordan (1994).

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992 and now share a 'Strategic Partnership', with defence and technology cooperation as central pillars.
Israel is a major supplier of defence equipment and technology to India, including missile defence systems and drones.
Growing cooperation in agricultural technology (drip irrigation, precision farming) and water management, areas of particular relevance to Indian agriculture.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A highly developed, innovation-driven economy despite limited natural resources, strong in technology, defence, agriculture, and pharmaceuticals.
Global leader in venture capital investment per capita and technology startup creation.
Major exporter of cut diamonds, high-tech equipment, and agricultural technology.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being called the 'Start-Up Nation' for its exceptional technology entrepreneurship density.
Pioneering drip irrigation and other arid-land agricultural technologies.
The historic revival of Hebrew as a modern spoken language.
Being at the centre of the long-running Israeli-Palestinian conflict and broader Middle East diplomacy.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Israel is a parliamentary democracy on the eastern Mediterranean, established in 1948, known globally for technology innovation and central to Middle East geopolitics.
keyFacts: Capital: Jerusalem (contested; most embassies historically in Tel Aviv). Currency: Israeli New Shekel.
Parliamentary democracy; unicameral Knesset; governed via Basic Laws rather than one written constitution.
Established in 1948 following a UN partition plan.
Known as the 'Start-Up Nation' for its technology sector.
commonConfusion: Israel has no single formal written constitution — it is governed through a series of 'Basic Laws' that function with constitutional status.

highYieldFacts: Israel: parliamentary democracy, established 1948, Knesset as its parliament.
Global tech innovation leader ('Start-Up Nation'); pioneered drip irrigation.
India-Israel: full diplomatic relations since 1992; major defence and agri-tech partnership.
commonTraps: Assuming Israel has a single written constitution — it relies on Basic Laws instead.
Overlooking that India-Israel diplomatic relations only formally began in 1992, despite older informal contacts.
mustRemember: Israel: parliamentary democracy since 1948, Start-Up Nation, key India defence/agri-tech partner since 1992.
